panels.label: Modeling Distortion at Front-End
panels.differs: baseline: only the FE model maps a standard signal to a distorted signal, with no predistortion or tuning

panels.label: Fine-tuning of NN-defined Modulator with NN-PD module
panels.differs: adds NN-PD and a fine-tuning algorithm that tunes the modulator and NN-PD so the fixed FE model outputs a compensated signal

content.key_idea: Inserting a fine-tuned NN-PD module between the modulator and a fixed FE model lets the pipeline learn a pre-distorted signal that cancels the front-end's modeled nonlinearity.
content.reading_order: Top panel first (FE Model alone), then down to the bottom chain: Modulator to NN-PD to fixed FE Model, fine-tuning arrows read last.

summary: Figure 11 contrasts two stacked block diagrams to motivate the paper's NN-PD fine-tuning mechanism. The top diagram, 'Modeling Distortion at Front-End,' shows a plain FE Model mapping a Standard signal to a Distorted signal, illustrating the RF front-end's nonlinearity in isolation. The bottom diagram, 'Fine-tuning of NN-defined Modulator with NN-PD module,' inserts a new NN-PD block between the NN-defined Modulator and a now-fixed FE Model; a Fine-tuning Algorithm box sends red arrows into both the Modulator and NN-PD to tune the modulator's kernels and the NN-PD's parameters. The red 'Pre-distorted signal' between NN-PD and the FE Model is deliberately distorted so the FE Model's fixed nonlinearity cancels it out, yielding the blue 'Compensated signal' at the output.
